column3: Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew calls them comforters of trouble; BSB says miserable comforters.
The Hebrew names wind-words and asks why you answer; BSB says long-winded speeches and continue testifying.
The Hebrew explicitly repeats soul for your position and mine; BSB says you were in my place.
The Hebrew names the movement of the lips; BSB calls it consolation.
The Hebrew asks what will leave me; BSB asks how it will go away.
The Hebrew names all my company; BSB says all my family.
The Hebrew describes shriveling me; BSB says You have bound me.
The Hebrew pictures sharpening his eyes against me; BSB says piercing me with His eyes.
The Hebrew has mouth and cheek in the singular; BSB uses mouths and cheeks.
The Hebrew names a wrongdoer in the singular; BSB says unjust men.

The Hebrew repeats breach; BSB says wound upon wound.

The Hebrew names the eyelids and death-shadow; BSB describes deep shadows around the eyes.

The Hebrew asks that there be no place for my cry; BSB describes the cry never being laid to rest.

The Hebrew has eye in the singular; BSB uses eyes.
The Hebrew describes one pleading for a man with God; BSB describes a man himself pleading with God.
The Hebrew says numbered years will come; BSB describes a few years having passed.
